## Statute
§3306(b)(10)(B)

## Reasoning
Section 3306(b)(10) excludes from the definition of "wages" payments made upon termination due to disability retirement, but only if those payments are made "under a plan established by the employer which makes provision for his employees generally" - this is the requirement of subsection (B).

The facts state that Alice paid Bob $12,980 after his disability retirement, but explicitly states that "Alice had no plan established to provide for her employees' disabilities."

Since §3306(b)(10)(B) requires the payment to be made under a plan established by the employer, and Alice had no such plan, the provision does NOT apply to this payment.

The claim states that §3306(b)(10)(B) applies to the payment. This is false given the statute requires an employer-established plan, which Alice did not have.

## Answer
Answer: Contradiction
